fields.Subskalen: (1) Fear of failure, (2) Probability of success, (3) Interest, (4) Challenge
fields.Validität: Findings on factorial and predictive validity; associations with later learning behaviour and learning performance; mean and correlation differences for different task types and learner types; high scale intercorrelations of the four factors.
fields.Normierung: None. Reference values: means and standard deviations.

sections.Kurzabstract: The FAM assesses current learning motivation and is used to measure learning and performance situations. It consists of four scales (fear of failure, interest, probability of success, challenge) with a total of 18 items. The starting point for the test construction was a study of the learning situation at the computer. Reliability: Internal consistencies according to Cronbach were between alpha = .66 and alpha = .90. Validity: Factorial validity was examined and yielded a four-factor structure with 58.4 % explained variance. Rheinberg and colleagues (2001) report that current motivation correlates with later learning behaviour and learning performance. Mean and correlation differences could be established for different task types and learner types. In addition, the test authors were able to demonstrate that the factors challenge and interest can predict performance, but these depend on the learning task and the number of learning trials. Calculations of the scale intercorrelations yielded high correlations, contrary to the assumption of independence of the four factors.
sections.Diagnostische Zielsetzung: The FAM assesses current learning motivation and is therefore used in studies for measuring learning and performance situations.
sections.Aufbau: The FAM consists of 18 items with a seven-point response format ("1 = trifft nicht zu" to "7 = trifft zu"), which are assigned to the four scales (1) fear of failure, (2) interest, (3) probability of success and (4) challenge.
sections.Grundlagen und Konstruktion: The instrument was conceived on the basis of classical test theory. The starting point was a study of the learning situation at the computer. Before working on the so-called "biology lab task", the FAM with 18 items was completed by 321 participants (students and upper-secondary school pupils; n = 184 female; mean age: 19 years). Its psychometric quality was examined (factor analysis, internal consistency, mean comparisons).
sections.Empirische Prüfung und Gütekriterien:
Reliability: Internal consistencies according to Cronbach were between alpha = .66 and alpha = .90.
Validity: Factorial validity was examined and yielded a four-factor structure with 58.4 % explained variance. Rheinberg and colleagues (2001) report that current motivation correlates with later learning behaviour and learning performance. Mean and correlation differences could be established for different task types and learner types. In addition, the test authors were able to demonstrate that the factors challenge and interest can predict performance, but these depend on the learning task and the number of learning trials.
Norms: The instrument is not normed. However, means and standard deviations from various samples are available.
sections.Testkonzept/Theoretischer Hintergrund:
The Fragebogen zur Erfassung der aktuellen Motivation (FAM) by Rheinberg, Vollmeyer and Burns (2001) was designed specifically for learning and performance situations. Current motivation arises from a motive (person factor) and an incentive (situation factor). An interaction and fit between person and situation factors yields the current motivation in the performance of behaviour (S. 57).
The aim of the instrument is to demonstrate effects of current motivation on learning and performance situations (Rheinberg et al., 2001. S. 58).
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungsmodus: Four scale means are calculated. A total score is not determined.
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungshilfen: Mean values are available that can be used as reference values (see under "Norming").
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungszeit: Only a few minutes are needed to calculate the four scale means. The FAM is used in performance situations that can last one to two hours (e.g. Vollmeyer et al., 2001).
sections.Durchführung/Testformen: Besides the German version, there is an American version, the Questionnaire of Current Motivation (QCM), with the factors Anxiety, Probability of Success, Interest and Challenge (Rheinberg et al., 2001, S. 59), as well as a Dutch version by Vellekoop (2008). The versions are to be administered in paper-pencil form. An adaptation by Winther (2007) consists of 16 items.
sections.Durchführung/Altersbereiche: A restriction of the age range is explicitly not made. So far, the FAM has been used with upper-secondary school pupils and students with a mean age of 19-21 years (Rheinberg et al., 2001, S. 58, S. 61, S. 62).
sections.Durchführung/Durchführungszeit: Completing the questionnaire with 18 items should take a few minutes.
sections.Durchführung/Material: The questionnaire is available as a paper-pencil version, for the completion of which a writing instrument is needed.
sections.Durchführung/Instruktion: The instruction is standardized and printed on the questionnaire.
sections.Durchführung/Durchführungsvoraussetzunge: The FAM is used only in connection with learning tasks in order to be able to draw conclusions about later performance from the motivational state assessed beforehand.
sections.Testkonstruktion: The instrument was conceived on the basis of classical test theory. The starting point was a study of a learning situation at the computer (Vollmeyer & Rheinberg, 1998). For this purpose, the questionnaire with 18 items was developed. 321 participants (students and upper-secondary school pupils; n = 184 female; mean age: 19 years) received the task instruction, completed the questionnaire and could then work on the so-called "biology lab task" (Rheinberg et al., 2001, S. 58, Vollmeyer & Rheinberg, 1998, 1999). Bachmann (2009) carried out an item analysis (discrimination & item difficulty) for two studies each and arrived at the following results: Discrimination varied strongly in the first study (pilot study) (rit = .08 to rit = .89), whereas the values in the main study varied comparatively less and were higher overall (rit = .34 to rit = .85). Item difficulty was, with a few exceptions, rather in the middle range (p = .31-.68).
sections.Gütekriterien/Objektivität: With regard to administration objectivity, it can be assumed that this is aimed at by the standardized instruction. Scoring objectivity should be ensured by the simple calculation of the scale means.
sections.Gütekriterien/Reliabilität: The German and American versions of the FAM were examined in different samples and task types. Internal consistencies according to Cronbach were between alpha = .66 and alpha = .90 for the German version and between alpha = .66 and alpha = .78 for the American version, whereby these turned out comparatively lower (Rheinberg et al., 2001, S. 60). Bachmann (2009, S. 99) reports values above alpha = .86 for the scales probability of success, fear of failure and interest, while alpha for challenge was alpha = .40. In a further study, the values were between alpha = .74 (challenge) and alpha = .91 (interest; S. 133).
sections.Gütekriterien/Validität:
Factorial validity was examined. A principal component analysis with varimax rotation yielded a four-factor structure with 58.4 % explained variance (Rheinberg et al., S. 59). Rheinberg and colleagues (2001) report that current motivation correlates with later learning behaviour and learning performance.
On the basis of seven samples, the following tasks were tested: "biology lab", inductive reasoning, analogy tasks, tangram, Tower of Hanoi and fleet manoeuvre. Mean differences could be demonstrated. For example, it was found that the probability of success was significantly lower for the Tower of Hanoi than for the fleet manoeuvre. The means of the scales challenge and probability of failure in the Tower of Hanoi task, in contrast, were significantly higher (Rheinberg et al., 2001, S. 60).
In two experiments (n = 45; n = 61), Rheinberg and colleagues (2001, S. 61 f.) were able to demonstrate that the factors challenge and interest can predict performance, but these depend on the learning task and the number of learning trials.
A comparison between fast and slow learners with regard to the correlation of the previously assessed FAM factors with final performance showed that the correlations of the slow learners in the factors interest and challenge differ significantly from those of the fast learners (Rheinberg et al., 2001, S. 63 f., see also Table 4, S. 64).
Bachmann (2009, S. 99) examined the scale intercorrelation of the four FAM scales in two studies. In the first study, probability of success correlated positively with interest and challenge at r = .78 and r = .61, respectively, while fear of failure correlated negatively with interest and probability of success at r = -.39 and r = -.43. Bachmann (2009, S. 100) points out that the values do not correspond to expectations: According to the cognitive-motivational process model, the factors should be independent of one another and should not correlate with one another. In the second study, the associations were similar but less pronounced (S. 134).
sections.Gütekriterien/Normierung:
The instrument is not normed. However, means and standard deviations from various samples are available (Rheinberg et al., 2001, Table 2, S. 60). They can be read off in Tables 1 and 2.

sections.Anwendungsmöglichkeiten: The FAM is suitable for use in studies with learning conditions for clarifying motivational research questions. It can serve for the statistical control of motivational effects (Rheinberg et al., 2001, S. 57).
sections.Bewertung:
The FAM was developed to assess current learning motivation and has been psychometrically examined. The findings show that, depending on task type and learner type, motivational states can differ, i.e. the FAM is sensitive with regard to the learning tasks and also varies depending on learner type (slow vs. fast learner). In particular the factors challenge and interest yielded predictively valid data with regard to learning performance. Internal consistency was examined. The assumed independence of the factors was refuted by the high scale intercorrelations.
The instrument allows conclusions about a person's motivational state from learning performance and, because of its economical application, is to be evaluated as very useful.

Study.Instructions: Nun wollen wir wissen, wie deine momentane Einstellung zu der beschriebenen Aufgabe ist. Dazu findest du auf dieser Seite Aussagen. Kreuze bitte jene Zahl an, die auf dich am Besten passt.

FAM01.Description: Ich mag solche Rätsel und Knobeleien.

FAM02.Description: Ich glaube, der Schwierigkeit dieser Aufgabe gewachsen zu sein.

FAM03.Description: Wahrscheinlich werde ich die Aufgabe nicht schaffen.

FAM04.Description: Bei der Aufgabe mag ich die Rolle des Wissenschaftlers, der Zusammenhänge entdeckt.

FAM05.Description: Ich fühle mich unter Druck, bei der Aufgabe gut abschneiden zu müssen.

FAM06.Description: Die Aufgabe ist eine richtige Herausforderung für mich.

FAM07.Description: Nach dem Lesen der Instruktion erscheint mir die Aufgabe sehr interessant.

FAM08.Description: Ich bin sehr gespannt darauf, wie gut ich hier abschneiden werde.

FAM09.Description: Ich fürchte mich ein wenig davor, dass ich mich hier blamieren könnte.

FAM10.Description: Ich bin fest entschlossen, mich bei dieser Aufgabe voll anzustrengen.

FAM11.Description: Bei Aufgaben wie dieser brauche ich keine Belohnung, sie machen mir auch so viel Spaß.

FAM12.Description: Es ist mir etwas peinlich, hier zu versagen.

FAM13.Description: Ich glaube, dass kann jeder schaffen.

FAM14.Description: Ich glaube, ich schaffe diese Aufgabe nicht.

FAM15.Description: Wenn ich die Aufgabe schaffe, werde ich schon ein wenig stolz auf meine Tüchtigkeit sein.

FAM16.Description: Wenn ich an die Aufgabe denke, bin ich etwas beunruhigt.

FAM17.Description: Eine solche Aufgabe würde ich auch in meiner Freizeit bearbeiten.

FAM18.Description: Die konkreten Leistungsanforderungen hier lähmen mich.
